searches.query: Can you send a rechargeable headlamp to Hawaii if I pay extra for fast shipping?

chunks.text: Delivery restrictions for rechargeable products  Products containing lithium batteries travel by ground service within the contiguous United States. The rule covers rechargeable lanterns, headlamps, power banks, and navigation devices, including products whose batteries are installed inside the equipment. These products cannot be sent by our air services, to Alaska or Hawaii, or to an international destination.  Selecting express shipping at checkout does not override this restriction. If a mixed order includes an ordinary item and a rechargeable device, the rechargeable item still travels by ground. A support agent must not promise that paying the express surcharge makes a battery shipment eligible for air transport. The customer can remove the battery product and place a separate order for the other items if those items qualify for the requested service.  Ground shipping has the delivery estimate shown at checkout for the destination. This policy does not supply a guaranteed arrival date for a particular parcel. Tracking events come from the carrier after dispatch.

International deliveries and returns  The store ships eligible ordinary products to Canada and the United Kingdom. International standard shipping costs USD 22 per order. Domestic membership and ordinary free-delivery thresholds do not apply to international shipping. Local import taxes and customs charges are paid by the recipient and are separate from the amount charged by the store.  Lithium-battery products, kayaks, and rigid roof cargo boxes are excluded from international delivery. An item being small enough to fit in a parcel does not remove a lithium-battery restriction. An international customer must not select a domestic destination as a placeholder and expect support to reroute a restricted product across the border.  Eligible international change-of-mind returns use the normal unused-condition and return-window rules. The customer arranges and pays the return transport. The store does not issue the USD 7 domestic return label for an international parcel. Import taxes are not refunded by the store.

Express order processing  Express delivery for eligible ordinary parcels costs USD 18. It has a two-business-day transit target after dispatch. Orders accepted before 13:00 Eastern Time on a business day are dispatched that day. Orders accepted at or after 13:00, or on a weekend, are dispatched on the next business day. Business days for this policy are Monday through Friday excluding published holidays.  The transit clock starts after dispatch, not when the customer adds an item to the basket. For an eligible order placed on a Monday at 14:00 during a week with no holidays, dispatch is Tuesday and the two-business-day transit target is Thursday. Payment review or an address problem can prevent dispatch until the issue is resolved. Do not infer that a particular order cleared those checks from this policy alone.  Some product categories cannot use express delivery. Check the lithium-delivery and oversize-delivery articles before promising this service.

Check the condition, return window, gift status, and transport restrictions separately. A lantern that contains a lithium battery still follows the battery shipping rules. The recipient of an eligible gift return receives store credit under the gift policy; allocation does not change that credit into a bank-card refund. Original shipping fees and a purchased return label remain separate from these item amounts.

Check the lithium-delivery and oversize-delivery articles before promising this service. A customer cannot pay a surcharge to remove a product restriction. The membership benefit covers qualifying standard delivery only. It does not discount the USD 18 express price or change the cutoff time.

Express service has its own price and restrictions; free standard delivery does not mean free express delivery. Any original outbound shipping charge remains separate from the item price when the customer later makes a change-of-mind return. The checkout presents the final delivery options before payment.

Swollen, leaking, or damaged rechargeable batteries  Stop using or charging a rechargeable device if its battery swells, leaks, or is visibly damaged. Do not send it through the ordinary returns process. The store's regular ground return label is not an approved way to ship a damaged battery. Contact the product safety team through the support form and choose the battery-safety category.  Provide the product model, purchase reference, a description of the damage, and photographs when it is safe to take them. The team gives the customer instructions for the specific product and location. Support agents must not improvise a packaging method or tell customers to remove a swollen battery. Follow the device manufacturer's safety instructions while waiting for the team.  The general shipping article permits certain undamaged battery products to travel by ground. That permission does not apply to a damaged battery. Whether the item qualifies for a warranty remedy is assessed separately from how it can be handled safely.

An international customer may use the return route if eligible and place a separate new order. Import taxes and international return transport are covered in the international-orders article. Exchange approval does not automatically waive a return-label fee.

Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service. A damaged, swollen, or leaking battery must never be sent using this ordinary label; use the damaged-battery procedure. Label creation does not count as dispatch. The parcel must actually be handed to the carrier within the return's dispatch deadline.

answer.answer: No, the rechargeable headlamp cannot be sent to Hawaii. Products containing lithium batteries, including headlamps, travel by ground service within the contiguous United States and cannot be sent to Alaska or Hawaii. Paying extra for express shipping does not override this restriction.
